key_insight: Normalizing Trajectory Models (NTM) replace each coarse reverse diffusion step with an expressive conditional normalizing flow, enabling few-step generation while retaining exact-likelihood training and expressive stepwise transitions.
problem_solved: Diffusion assumptions break down when generation is compressed to few coarse steps; prior few-step solutions (distillation, consistency, adversarial) lose the likelihood framework. NTM restores principled likelihood-based training for compressed/few-step sampling.
method: Model every reverse transition as a conditional normalizing flow conditioned on the next state and timestep, giving each coarse step high expressivity.
Train the sequence of flows with exact maximum likelihood across steps, preserving tractable likelihoods and stable optimization.
Learn compressed trajectories that summarize many small denoising steps into a few learned expressive transitions to enable fast, few-step sampling.
impact: NTM provides a practical path to fast few-step generation without abandoning likelihood-based evaluation, so practitioners can get efficient sampling and principled density estimates simultaneously—useful for research, model selection, and production deployment.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: standard diffusion (many small Gaussian denoising steps) vs NTM (few expressive flow-based transitions).
Block diagram showing a conditional normalizing flow at one reverse step (inputs: noisy state + timestep; outputs: cleaner state) with exact likelihood annotation.
Line/chart showing trade-off curves: sample quality and log-likelihood as a function of number of steps, highlighting NTM improvement at low step counts.
Trajectory visualization: animated or stacked states showing compressed learned transitions vs many small denoising steps.
paper_authors: Jiatao Gu, Tianrong Chen, Ying Shen, David Berthelot, Shuangfei Zhai
